name: Guevarism
summary: Guevarism is the revolutionary Marxism-Leninism associated with Che Guevara: armed insurrection by a small guerrilla vanguard (the foco) can create the conditions for revolution, especially in the rural periphery. It couples this with proletarian internationalism, hard anti-imperialism, state-led socialist construction, and moral rather than material incentives to forge a selfless 'New Man'.
scope: The mature thought of Che Guevara (c. 1959-1967): Guerrilla Warfare, 'Guerrilla war, a method', 'Socialism and Man in Cuba', the Algiers speech and the Message to the Tricontinental, plus the foco doctrine as described in the scholarship. It excludes later Latin American guerrilla movements and neo-Guevarist currents, whose positions on elections, gender and culture differ.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Free universal health care was a flagship social achievement of the Cuban revolution Guevara helped lead, and he served as a revolutionary health worker; socialism for him means ending exploitation in basic services.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Not addressed directly; a socialist aimed at ending exploitation would back higher wages, though he stressed moral over wage incentives in building socialism.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: He called the law of value an invisible tether of capitalism and rejected using capitalist levers like individual material interest as a road to a blind alley.

public-ownership.rationale: As Cuban industry minister he nationalised and planned major industries; socialism meant abolishing exploitation, which requires social ownership of the means of production.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Taxation levels are not discussed; his egalitarian aims imply support, but his programme went beyond taxes to expropriation.

unions-good.rationale: Not a theme of his writings; he valued organised workers and voluntary labour but subordinated mass organisations to the party and revolutionary leadership.

property-fundamental.rationale: Cuban revolution expropriated large estates and enterprises; socialism for him ends exploitation, so private property cannot be a near-inviolable right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Wants imperialist monopolies defeated or expelled rather than regulated, so mild agreement with the direction of the statement at most.

cut-welfare.rationale: He sought to remove material deprivation and build solidarity as a duty; cutting welfare contradicts the socialist aims he stated.

worker-ownership.rationale: He favoured state/social ownership with workers' consciousness and participation rather than syndicalist enterprise ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed; revolutionaries accepted vigilance against counterrevolution, but no stated position on terror surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; Guevara's stress on revolutionary moral discipline suggests scepticism, but he left no position.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed in sources; no stated line on legal speech restrictions of this kind.

strong-leader.rationale: Believed in the dialectical unity of leader and masses and in a leading vanguard, but he spoke of leading by example rather than bypassing gridlock.

state-harmful.rationale: He wanted a revolutionary state and party to build socialism and defend against imperialism; he did not seek abolition of the state.

limit-guns.rationale: His strategy rests on arming the people and guerrilla forces; arms for liberation movements should not be commodities.

empower-police-military.rationale: He distrusted standing armies of the old order and favoured a people's army, though revolutionary defence needs strength.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not discussed; adherents' revolutionary moral austerity and egalitarian aims point different ways.

decide-locally.rationale: He called for institutions linking government and community, but revolution was directed by a centralised vanguard and leadership.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not a theme; the New Man ideal of transformation through education favours rehabilitation, but revolutionary justice under Guevara was severe.

traditional-family.rationale: Guevara described the revolutionary as sacrificing family comforts for the cause and aimed at a new society; no endorsement of traditional family as foundation.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Cuban revolution of his time was hostile to homosexuality and he left no considered view; anachronistic question.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed by Guevara; anachronistic and split among later Guevarists.

more-religion-public.rationale: Materialist Marxist-Leninist base; he contrasted his humanism with Christian and philanthropic humanism.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Anti-colonial and anti-imperialist, condemning exploitation of oppressed peoples; racial redress policy is not specifically his topic.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed in his writings; no position on gender theory.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He valued anti-imperialist national liberation yet aimed at an internationalist New Man and free artistic inquiry, not heritage preservation.

gradual-change.rationale: Rejects waiting and reformism; insurrection can itself create the conditions and armed struggle is the main road.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Internationalist ethos favours solidarity across borders; immigration policy is not addressed.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He saw international bodies as dominated by imperial powers; he preferred solidarity between peoples and socialist states.

free-trade.rationale: He said trade at world-market prices between socialist and poor countries made the former accomplices of imperialist exploitation, and saw capitalism as exploiting dependent countries.

nation-first.rationale: He held that a death for another country's liberation advances one's own and demanded proletarian internationalism.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: He opposed imperialist military power, though he supported revolutionary internationalist armed solidarity, a different logic from rights-based intervention.

open-borders.rationale: Internationalism and international proletarian armies imply no value in borders, but he did not advocate open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: He sought rapid socialist development and industrialisation and saw underdevelopment as the product of exploitation.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; no stated views, though he blamed capitalism and imperialism for global ills.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: He expected new technology to help shape the 21st-century human but held that consciousness, not technology alone, was decisive.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic for a 1960s revolutionary; nothing in his writings bears on nuclear power.

revolution-justified.rationale: Armed revolution is the core of Guevarism; he held liberation would come through armed struggle in most cases.

experts-over-public.rationale: He prized mass consciousness and leader-mass unity, and the vanguard leads by example; technocracy as such not endorsed.

central-planning.rationale: He ran the Cuban industrial ministry on budgetary-finance planning and rejected market levers, though planning problems were acknowledged.

socialized-markets.rationale: He rejected commodity relations and the law of value as tools during the transition, which excludes market socialism.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not a Guevarist position; agrarian questions were handled by land reform.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Egalitarian anti-exploitation aim implies agreement, but he went beyond taxation to abolition of private accumulation.

basic-income.rationale: Work as social duty and moral incentive are central; unconditional payments conflict with his view of labour as self-expression.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: He advocated industrialisation of dependent economies and attacked unequal exchange, which favours protection, though not as tariff doctrine.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He directed Cuban industrialisation by state planning and stressed development paid for collectively.

widespread-small-property.rationale: He aimed at socialism with social ownership, though he backed peasant demands and land reform for peasant support.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Wanted work freed from being a sale of labour power and advocated moral incentives, with communism as a distant spiritual rebirth in attitudes to work.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Opposes market money; he headed Cuba's national bank, a state instrument.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not his model; he wanted a party-led vanguard and mass organisations, not employer-labour bodies.

one-party-rule.rationale: He described the party as a vanguard of the best workers, ideologically ahead of the masses; Cuba's single-party practice was supported, though the foco often substituted for a party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Anti-feudal and anti-oligarchic revolutionary; monarchy would be incompatible with socialist revolution.

democracy-best.rationale: He rejected transplanting bourgeois democracy and warned that elections may merely renew oligarchic rule, though he allowed combative peaceful politics where legality exists.

direct-votes.rationale: He wanted new institutions linking government and community but did not advocate referendums on laws.

workers-councils.rationale: He rejected parliamentary forms but placed leadership in the vanguard party and state, not councils as the basis of power.

right-to-secede.rationale: Not addressed; anti-imperialist self-determination but continental unity of struggle.

natural-rulers.rationale: Not elitist by birth, but leaders and the vanguard are those most advanced by conscious sacrifice.

political-violence-never.rationale: Held that violence is a legitimate tool of the exploited and called for it to be used decisively.

war-builds-character.rationale: He described hatred and a tough war as forging fighters and the New Man, and accepted a long cruel war.

separate-church-state.rationale: Marxist-Leninist secularism, though Guevara himself did not centre this issue.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Materialist; his humanism is explicitly distinct from Christian humanism.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Wholly at odds with his statism and people's army.

military-superiority.rationale: He wanted the revolutionary side to win protracted war against imperialism; superiority as such not discussed.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Internationalist; he called for international proletarian armies and rejected ethnic exclusivity.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Marxism-Leninism base; class perspective is central to his humanism and revolutionary analysis.

equal-outcomes.rationale: His goal is abolishing exploitation and distribution by need in communism, though he allowed differences in the transition.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Tied peasants and land reform; indigenous autonomy was not addressed.

colonial-reparations.rationale: He condemned colonial and imperialist exploitation and urged renegotiating oppressive debts, but did not frame reparations.

civilizational-union.rationale: He proposed class and continental anti-imperial unity, not unions of shared religion or civilization.

self-interest-moral.rationale: He called capitalist individual material interest a blind alley, and stressed sacrifice and duty.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Work as social duty and sacrifice as conscious payment toward freedom; he saw the individual as more complete under socialism through that social tie.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed; Marxist tradition rejects population explanations of poverty.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Pro-industrialisation Marxism; he saw capitalist imperialism, not industry, as the problem.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Mentions new technology shaping the new man, but not a disruption doctrine.

human-enhancement.rationale: He wrote of shaping a new human through education and work, not technological enhancement, so no stance can be inferred.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; rule by conscious leaders and masses.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Anachronistic; his texts say nothing about state access to private communications.

restore-past-order.rationale: Revolutionary and forward-looking; creates a new man and a new society.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Pragmatic in tactics but explicitly ideological in aims; he insisted on consciousness rather than whatever works.

direct-action.rationale: Armed action over elections and parliament, with allowance for combative electoral politics where the democratic orientation is intact; strikes and protests were considered insufficient.

means-match-ends.rationale: He accepted violence, hatred and coercion (moral compulsion) as means to a humane end, though he insisted on moral example.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Wants industrialised socialism and the human being of the 21st century.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: He sought to free work from alienation and make it self-expression, but made no call to abolish division of labour.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Communism as the horizon with moral incentives; distribution by need ultimately, with a transition.

production-for-use.rationale: He rejected commodity logic and profit as organising principles of the economy.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Capitalist wealth rests on the exploitation of workers and dependent countries; socialism is the abolition of exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: He endorsed the term, applying it to individuals of the winning class as well as the former rulers.

collective-farming.rationale: He favoured peasant alliance and agrarian reform in the guerrilla stage; collectivisation was not his focus.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Imperialism as the last stage of capitalism and a world system that must be defeated confrontationally.

taxation-theft.rationale: Opposes the libertarian view in a statist socialism.

harm-principle.rationale: He saw coercion by moral compulsion and revolutionary duty as acceptable.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Collective duty and class perspective take precedence over liberal individual rights.

conscription.rationale: He built a people's army and revolution relied on mobilised citizens; formal conscription not discussed.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Foreign to Guevarism; he stressed the revolutionary duty to the community.

positive-liberty.rationale: He said liberation from alienation and capitalist necessity is needed to reclaim human nature through liberated labour and culture.

media-academia-power.rationale: He located power in imperialist states and local oligarchies, not in universities or media.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Antiracist Marxist humanism holds ability gaps are social.

organic-representation.rationale: Rejects parliamentary parties but via vanguard party, not corporate bodies.

total-state.rationale: Party and state led the economy and education in his model, but he opposed dogmatic cultural control, rejecting socialist realism.

national-rebirth.rationale: He called for a New Man, but not national decadence and rebirth.

territorial-expansion.rationale: He framed imperialism as the enemy to be defeated worldwide, so a strong state expanding its reach is the opposite of his aims.

bound-labor.rationale: He criticised feudal rural conditions and sought land for peasants.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Marxist class perspective sees ideas as class-shaped, though he did not argue this epistemology.

universal-morality.rationale: Appeals to a humanist morality and love for humanity but grounded in class perspective rather than universal reason.

single-common-good.rationale: Class struggle denies a neutral common good, yet a communist society aims at a unified good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed by his writings; he visited Israel early on but is not recorded to have taken a stated position.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: His writings never address diaspora return or citizenship; nothing can be inferred.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is outside his writings, which focus on class and imperialism.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Wanted worker participation tied to consciousness but within a state-planned vanguard-led economy.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education was to be a state tool for creating the new human.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Orthodox fiscal prudence was not his concern; state-led development is.

economic-freedom.rationale: Rejects market freedom as basis of liberty; capitalism binds people to the law of value.

rule-by-example.rationale: The party leads by example and the revolutionary must set an example by sacrifice; vanguard of best workers.

national-self-determination.rationale: Supports anti-colonial national liberation, but sees it as part of continental and international struggle.

force-without-un.rationale: He expected no legality from imperialist-dominated institutions, but this reads about revolutionary armed solidarity.

reason-over-faith.rationale: He prized cold intelligence along with love and conviction.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Work is a social duty but welfare is not a conditional benefit in his scheme.

class-collaboration.rationale: He judged the national bourgeoisie unable to resist imperialism and class struggle central.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: He criticised dogmatic cultural control but did not promote destroying heritage.

dominated-front.rationale: He called for an anti-imperialist front of dominated peoples and continents and urged Vietnams everywhere.

workers-nation.rationale: Proletarian internationalism is a moral duty and practical necessity.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Egalitarian New Man; women's roles in guerrilla and revolution; not directly addressed.

ban-interest.rationale: He attacked commodity relations but never discussed usury or interest bans.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxist-Leninist view of the state as class rule, with the proletarian dictatorship using it for the revolutionary class.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Anachronistic; he wanted industrial development of dependent economies.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy at odds with class analysis.

proportional-representation.rationale: He called electoral politics insufficient and didn't take sides on voting systems.

national-mission.rationale: Anti-imperialist; nations should not export their system by state power, though revolution should be exported through internationalism.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: He portrayed oligarchies using democracy as a mask and local bourgeoisies as servants of imperialism.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Anti-eugenic; belief in the human being shaped by society.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Revolutionary justice and executions under him; he left no stated view on accountability for security forces.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Humanism of a proletarian class perspective, universal liberation from exploitation, though class enemies are treated as targets.

socialism-one-country.rationale: He warned that without proletarian internationalism revolution falls into complacency and wanted worldwide confrontation with imperialism.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not addressed directly; strongly anti-colonial in general.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Religious personal law is not discussed; his secular socialism gives no clear rule.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not a concern, but secular and unfriendly to clerical power.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Indian religious question unrelated to materialist socialism.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Materialist education for the new human; no explicit statement.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Socialist states must stay united and prepared against imperialism; he did not discuss withering away.

consent-of-governed.rationale: He required popular support for guerrilla success but legitimacy came from revolution rather than consent procedure.

trade-surplus.rationale: Criticised unequal exchange on world-market terms rather than mercantilism.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Armed struggle and violence are legitimate tools of the exploited.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: No stated view; he rejected bourgeois legality as an end in itself, but did not discuss banning parties.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: His view of freedom as ending exploitation and imperialism is close in spirit.

separated-powers.rationale: He rejected transplanting bourgeois legislative chambers and sought unity of government and community.

vanguard-party.rationale: The party is a minority of the best workers, ideologically ahead of the masses, leading by example; the guerrilla is the combat vanguard.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The guerrilla and revolution aim at the rural poor and exploited peoples as the revolutionary force.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Not addressed; socialist public ownership leans against.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: He saw strikes as insufficient for revolution but not as to be restricted.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: He attributed poverty to exploitation and imperialist domination.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: His internationalism and calls for peoples to unite across borders imply that diversity is no obstacle to solidarity.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Revolutionary defence justified harsh measures; no specific statement on legal protections.

party-controls-media.rationale: He criticised dogmatic socialist realism and urged free artistic inquiry, but was a Cuban state official under party control.

party-commands-army.rationale: Guerrillas were led by political-military leaders and party guidance; not stated as doctrine.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: His internationalism implies hostility to barriers between peoples, but he did not discuss naturalization.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: His revolutionary asceticism and leaders' sacrifice imply support; no stated policy.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Revolutionary discipline and vanguard party; not discussed explicitly.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Supranational unions in Europe are not addressed; he preferred anti-imperialist continental unity.

head-commands-forces.rationale: He favoured a people's army guided by revolutionary leadership; the command of forces by a head of state is not discussed.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is outside his writings.

clerical-rule.rationale: A materialist Marxist-Leninist who set his humanism apart from Christian humanism would reject rule by clergy.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Not addressed in this form; his stance in inter-imperialist war is not stated.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: He criticised socialist realism and called for free artistic inquiry, though he held art must serve the new man.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits are not discussed; his vanguard model does not turn on electoral terms.

recall-officials.rationale: He wanted closer links between government and community but did not propose recall of officials.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He favoured socialist unity and alliance against imperialism.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Housing tenure is not discussed in the sources.

people-in-arms.rationale: He held that popular forces can defeat a regular army and urged arming the people.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The countryside is the primary arena of struggle, not morally healthier.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: He saw the Geneva division of Vietnam as imposed and supported anti-imperial liberation.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Intellectuals must join and be led by the people but peasants need leadership from intellectuals.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: He opposed imperialist domination but made no claim about cultures being equal or different.

death-penalty.rationale: He oversaw revolutionary executions as acceptable against counterrevolutionaries, though not as an anti-terror policy.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: His texts do not address school curricula on sex or gender.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: His materialist education for the new human would exclude religious doctrines in science teaching.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed; revolutionary austerity and artistic freedom pull in different directions.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not discussed; no basis in his writings for an answer.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: He stressed the social unity of the individual and mass; but also free artistic inquiry.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: He urged developing countries to force renegotiation of oppressive foreign debts.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: He said colonial status is a consequence of imperialist domination, and local bourgeoisies are parasitic, so independence needs socialist change.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Not addressed; revolution rather than assembly.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Revolutionary leaders accepted moral compulsion, but he did not state this trade-off directly.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Socialist states have an international duty to help finance development of poor countries.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: He made no statement on national nuclear arsenals, though he was hostile to imperialist military dominance.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Electoral design is not discussed; he doubted that elections change oligarchic rule.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial compromise is not discussed beyond his criticism of the Geneva partition of Vietnam.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Socialist property exists to end exploitation and serve society; he rejects an absolute right.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: He criticised the Soviets over aid, trade and the Sino-Soviet feud, but did not call them capitalist.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Anachronistic; environmental regulation is not in his writings.

collective-defense.rationale: He demanded socialist states accept the risk of treating attacks on a socialist state as attacks on all.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Not discussed in general terms; he opposed imperialist aggression.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: He did not discuss church property or clergy; a socialist state would plausibly curb them, but this is unstated.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Secession is not discussed; revolutionary self-determination and state unity point different ways.

character-from-environment.rationale: The New Man is created through education, daily action and new social foundations.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: He never wrote on rulers and law; his leaders are meant to lead by example and unity with the masses.

space-expansion.rationale: Anachronistic; his writings do not touch on space.

leader-cult.rationale: He insisted on the dialectical unity of leader and masses; cult was not his idea.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family law is not addressed in his writings.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: He accepted that classes and bourgeois remnants persisted in the transition, but did not take this specific line.

land-redistribution.rationale: Tied guerrillas, peasants and land reform together; peasant demands such as land need meeting.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed; no basis in his texts for a firm position.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: A materialist and secular revolutionary would not support punishing leaving a religion.

women-must-cover.rationale: Compelled dress codes conflict with his emphasis on liberation and free human development.

common-currency.rationale: Monetary unions are not addressed; he stressed continental anti-imperial unity politically.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: He supported Latin American continental struggle, not ancestry-based union.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: He held that socialism must rest on solidarity, duty and moral incentives, and rejected capitalist individual interest as the lever of progress.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: He backed state control of the economy and distribution, but never addressed price ceilings for scarce foods specifically.

moral-incentives.rationale: Guevara said the main tool of building socialism must be moral in character, warning that reliance on individual material interest leads to a blind alley.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The foco doctrine holds that insurrection itself can create the subjective conditions for a broader uprising.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Not addressed; Guevara's internationalism and focus on class and anti-imperialist unity suggest a common socialist state rather than institutionalised minority self-government, inferred from Socialism and Man in Cuba.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not addressed directly; his internationalist call to fight oppression wherever one lives, rather than withdraw to a separate homeland, is the basis of this inference.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: As a Marxist-Leninist he saw socialism as grounded in economic structures, but he stressed consciousness and the will of the vanguard, so he sat well short of strict determinism.

ban-cartels.rationale: Not addressed; he rejected capitalist competition as a goal and favoured state planning, so antitrust to protect markets was not his concern.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from his hostility to capitalist firms and banks, where he would favour state ownership rather than rescuing private owners with public money, though a socialist state aiding its own enterprises is not a bailout.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Not addressed; he distrusted bourgeois legal institutions but also placed the vanguard and party above simple majority rule, so the question fits poorly.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Gender quotas were not discussed; inferred from socialist commitment to women's participation in the revolution, which he praised in guerrilla writings.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: He wanted trade on non-exploitative terms among socialist and developing countries and urged a common socialist bloc and internationalism, not autarky.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Not addressed; he condemned unequal trade terms, but binding standards in trade pacts belong to a later era of liberal trade policy.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Eliminating class privilege and exploitation was the core of his socialism, so rank by birth is plainly rejected.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Inferred from Guevara's internationalism, which rejects the nation as the centre of loyalty.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Guevara condemned imperialism and colonial rule in every form, and called for the people of the periphery to fight it.

patriotic-education.rationale: Guevara taught proletarian internationalism and a socialist New Man instead of national pride, though Cuban education also stressed revolutionary patriotism.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred: a revolutionary egalitarian outlook leaning to support race-conscious remedies, though Guevara did not address the issue directly.

public-money-creation.rationale: Inferred: Guevara ran the national bank and a centrally planned economy, so the state controlled money and credit.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Guevara held that capitalism was in decline and tied to imperialist wars, and that the revolution would end it.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred from his anti-imperialism, which denies any claim built on past imperial rule.

delink-world-market.rationale: Guevara said socialist trade with poor countries at world-market prices was exploitation, but he sought socialist-bloc ties and not autarky.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Split: his call for armed struggle in the periphery implies the rich-world working class was not the main force, but he held to proletarian internationalism.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred from his socialism: private owners have no right to exclude, and the revolution sought to end such discrimination.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Guevara dismissed bourgeois legality and put revolutionary power above formal constitutional limits.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Hard anti-imperialism and neocolonialism critique imply colonial borders are illegitimate; inferred.

elective-rulers.rationale: Guevara rejected bourgeois electoralism and saw legitimacy through revolution and the vanguard; inferred.

minority-veto.rationale: The vanguard party and democratic centralism override individual dissent; inferred.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Guevara held that when a government comes to power by fraud or force, armed struggle is justified; inferred.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Guevara viewed bourgeois parliaments as limited and relied on a vanguard party and armed struggle.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Guevara called for solidarity and duty among equals and a transformed society, not paternalism from the privileged; inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The New Man is defined by duty to society and revolutionary activity.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Guevara criticised bourgeois culture and art as alienating; inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Guevara notes that the ruling class uses ideology and institutions but stresses force; inferred.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Guevara's Algiers speech attacks unequal exchange between poor and rich countries as exploitation.

native-born-offices.rationale: Proletarian internationalism rejects native-only privilege, but not addressed directly.

party-own-road.rationale: Guevara stressed internationalism and criticised Soviet policy, but not on party independence directly.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Guevara held that socialist countries have a duty to give development aid, and stressed internationalism.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; Guevara stressed class over ethnic leadership.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Guevara was anti-fascist as a communist; the point is inferred.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Guevarism is Marxism-Leninism; it rejects equating communism with fascism.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Revolutionary outlook favours removing symbols of oppressors; inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed in the sources opened; left neutral as no position can be inferred from the ideology's principles.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed in the sources opened; left neutral as no position can be inferred from the ideology's principles.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Guevara's Marxism was universalist, but he emphasised Latin American conditions; split.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Guevara viewed the guerrilla army as a political vanguard, but not as guardian of a bourgeois constitution; inferred.

paid-care-work.rationale: Not addressed; Guevara stressed voluntary labour.

missingStatements.text: Material incentives should be replaced as the main spur to work by moral incentives and a sense of social duty.
missingStatements.rationale: Guevara said the main tool of building socialism must be moral in character, warning that reliance on individual material interest leads to a blind alley.

missingStatements.text: A small armed group can create the conditions for revolution rather than waiting for them to appear.
missingStatements.rationale: The foco doctrine holds that insurrection itself can create the subjective conditions for a broader uprising.

missingStatements.text: Rich or socialist countries trading with poor countries at world-market prices take part in exploiting them.
missingStatements.rationale: In Algiers Guevara called socialist countries trading at world-market prices accomplices in imperialist exploitation.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to Guevara's Algiers speech; the underlying claim is covered by sovereign-debt-cancellation, colonial-reparations and rich-countries-aid-poor.

missingStatements.text: Building a new society requires creating a new kind of person with different values, not only new economic structures.
missingStatements.rationale: The New Man is central to his argument that socialism needs a change in consciousness alongside economic foundations.

notes: Guevara allowed peaceful, combative electoral politics where democratic legality exists, so answers on democracy are moderate. Many social questions (gender, sexuality, religion policy, environment) were not addressed and are low confidence.
